home.title: One map. Two observatories.
home.intro: Dhofar Agro & Eco Observatory turns open Earth-observation into interpretable satellite decisions for Dhofar: Agricultural Observation Units (AOUs) across the Najd irrigated plain, and restoration status for the fog mountains. Partners may act on Analysis / Decision / Seed with zero field visits. Gallery STAC refresh updates scene listings only; AOU/MPI layers stay provisional until a full monitor run.
home.whyBody: Irrigated blocks in Najd are large enough for 10 m pixels. Optical VNIR + SWIR supports vegetation and canopy-moisture indices. Inland Najd is hyper-arid, so clear scenes are common most months. Mountain Khareef seasons need cloud-aware composites and moisture persistence — not a single post-rain image.
home.seasonBody: Najd wheat: typical sowing early–mid November; harvest from early April. Mountain restoration follows a dynamic Khareef calendar (Pre → Onset → Peak → Weakening → End → Post) — seeding windows are site- and moisture-dependent, not a fixed date.
home.agroBody: Detect and monitor cultivated activity as AOUs (e.g. AOU-NJ-000184). Day-one operation does not require official farm names. Alerts map bare · healthy · water_attention · vigor_attention into health and water labels. Biotic risk uses possible_biotic_stress only — never pest certainty.
home.restoBody: Site suitability with a separate confidence score, Moisture Persistence Index class, regeneration ladder (Protect → ANR → Enrichment → Active Planting → Avoid), and fog-escarpment species such as Terminalia dhofarica. Arid Najd species are not auto-mixed onto fog slopes.
home.previewNote: Imagery can refresh the Sentinel-2 scene list from Planetary Computer STAC. AOU alerts, mountain MPI, and restoration scores remain offline / provisional stubs — not recomputed by that button.

analysis.title: Agricultural analysis
analysis.blurb: Four-level satellite decision support for Najd Agricultural Observation Units: overview, spatial, temporal, and provisional decision scores. Thresholds follow SCIENCE_LOCKS expert v1. A field visit is not required to use this page.
analysis.ndviDesc: Green biomass, phenology, crop vs bare, failed plantings (flat/low curve).
analysis.saviDesc: Sparse canopy over bright desert soil; reduces soil noise versus NDVI.
analysis.ndmiDesc: Canopy water / irrigation stress through the season. Spectral moisture proxy ≠ field soil moisture.
analysis.establishedDesc: NDVI rises by Dec–Jan and peaks Feb–Mar above bare/neighbor thresholds.
analysis.sparseDesc: Weak or delayed green-up; high within-field NDVI variance.
analysis.irrigationDesc: NDVI OK early, NDMI drops mid-season; often warmer than peers.
analysis.salinityDesc: Chronically low peak NDVI; high salinity proxies on fallow scenes — needs field EC.
analysis.abandonedDesc: Persistent bare signature across winter while neighbors green.
analysis.compareBody: March peak-wheat scenes show bright NDVI on active pivots. Late-summer scenes return to bare desert reflectance — useful for abandoned vs cropped contrast.

issues.d: Late sowing after early Nov cuts yield; low/late Dec–Jan NDVI rise.
Mid-season NDMI drop; early senescence; warmer Landsat LST vs neighbors.
Reduced peak NDVI and bare-soil salinity indices — calibrate with EC samples.
Bare all winter while adjacent fields green.
Circular NDVI rings or pie wedges of low vigor.
Unusual spatial/temporal spectral anomaly vs peers — satellite attention only; never confirm pest/disease from space. Optional additional field verification (last resort) only.

about.title: Method & scientific honesty
about.blurb: Dhofar Agro & Eco Observatory (مرصد ظفار الزراعي البيئي) is a bilingual agricultural and restoration observatory for Dhofar, Oman (product spec v1.0.1).
about.aoiBody: Agricultural: Najd farm corridor ≈ [53.4, 17.5, 54.3, 18.5] (Thumrait, Shisr, Hanfit, Saih Al-Khairat; Al-Mazyunah west). Restoration: Jabal Qara, Samhan, Qamar; Mirbat and Mughsayl foothills.
about.sensorsBody: Primary: Sentinel-2 L2A. Backup: Landsat 8/9. Context only (not field-scale soil moisture): SMAP / ESA CCI, CHIRPS, ERA5. Mountain MVP adds DEM wetness proxies and expert Site×Species rules.
workflow: Detect agricultural footprint → segment AOUs (not official farms until cadastral link).
Mask clouds/shadows (SCL); extract NDVI / NDMI (+ optional NDRE) time series.
Map bare / healthy / water_attention / vigor_attention to interpretive health & water labels.
For mountains: Khareef staging, MPI, hydrology screen, suitability vs confidence, action ladder.
Optional additional field verification (last resort) only if someone later logs a seeding event — never a prerequisite.
honesty: No confirmed pest/disease diagnosis from space — use Possible Biotic Stress. Field visit is not required to act.
NDMI / MPI are proxies — not plot-level soil moisture meters.
SMAP / CCI / ERA5 / CHIRPS are regional context only.
Suitability Score and Confidence Score stay separate.

Fog-escarpment species (e.g. Terminalia dhofarica) are not mixed with arid Najd species by default: samr (Vachellia tortilis, syn. Acacia tortilis), sidr (Ziziphus spina-christi), ghaf (Prosopis cineraria).
AOU ≠ Official Farm until authorized government data is linked.
about.limitBody: This MVP can refresh the Imagery STAC scene list from Planetary Computer. AOU alert GeoJSON and mountain MPI remain offline or illustrative stubs. It does not recompute live post-khareef MPI or print Environment Authority approval. A field visit is not required to use Najd Analysis / Decision / Seed.
about.dataSourcesBody: Sentinel-2 L2A via Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC; static browse previews; sample mountain GeoJSON. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (ESA).
howToRead: AOU ≠ farm — Agricultural Observation Units are satellite cells, not official farm names or cadastral boundaries.
STAC ≠ monitoring — Gallery «Refresh scene list from STAC» updates imagery listings only; it does not recompute AOU alerts or farm monitor layers.
MPI stub — Mountain Moisture Persistence (MPI) classes on sample sites are provisional stubs; this MVP does not compute live MPI.
Suitability ≠ Confidence — restoration suitability and confidence stay separate scores and are never merged into one number.

Mountain seeding Hold — post-khareef MPI (2026-09-15–2026-10-31) plus Agrofostery SHA is required before seeding recommendations. Status view is allowed now. This is not an official planting plan and not EA-approved.

footer: Dhofar Agro & Eco Observatory · open-data observatory MVP · satellite-first decisions; field visit is last-resort optional verification

honesty.title: Data honesty
honesty.cloud: Cloud cover is reported per scene; peak-Khareef mountain scenes may be cloudy — SCL masking applies where computed.
honesty.proxy: NDVI/NDMI (and mountain MPI) are satellite proxies — not plot-level soil moisture meters. NDMI ≠ field soil moisture.
honesty.pest: No confirmed pest/disease diagnosis from space — use “Possible Biotic Stress”. Optional additional field verification (last resort) only.
honesty.aou: AOU ≠ official farm boundary until authorized cadastral link.
honesty.stale: Scenes always show last-updated. Empty STAC results fail visibly — never silent reuse of stale imagery without a stamp.
honesty.mountain: Mountain suitability / confidence / MPI on sample sites are illustrative stubs — farm STAC refresh does not compute live mountain MPI.
honesty.stac: Gallery STAC refresh ≠ AOU/MPI recompute — scene list only.

simple.guideTitle: Understand your land, one step at a time
simple.guideIntro: Choose an area, check when it was observed, then read what the satellite suggests. You do not need to know the technical terms.

choose.title: 1. Find an area
choose.body: Open the agricultural map and select a coloured cell. The current monitoring window covers only part of Dhofar.

read.title: 2. Read the observation
read.body: Check the image date and evidence quality before interpreting a colour or a number.

act.title: 3. Follow up
act.body: Compare later observations. A satellite flag is a reason to investigate, not an automatic irrigation or pesticide instruction.

labels.healthy: Vegetation: no flag in this observation

readings.healthy: The observation did not trigger the model’s stress rules. This does not confirm that plants are free of disease or that irrigation is sufficient.
readings.bare: Little green vegetation was detected. This may be normal for a fallow field or the current season; it is not proof of crop failure.
readings.water_attention: The satellite shows a moisture-related signal that deserves attention. It is not a direct measurement of soil moisture or irrigation need.
readings.vigor_attention: A vegetation signal deserves attention. Season, harvest, water stress and other factors may explain it.
readings.unclear: A current conclusion is not supported by enough usable data. Clouds, incomplete coverage or retained older readings may be involved.

actions.healthy: Continue monitoring and compare with the next usable observation.
actions.bare: Consider the planting or harvest season before interpreting this as a problem.
actions.water_attention: Compare with earlier readings and, if possible, check local irrigation conditions before changing watering.
actions.vigor_attention: Compare the dates and neighbouring areas. Optional local observations can help explain the change.
actions.unclear: Keep the last trusted observation in view and wait for a usable update.

aou.title: What is a monitoring area (AOU)?
aou.body: An area grouped from satellite observations for repeated monitoring. It is not an official farm boundary, land title or ownership record.

ndvi.title: NDVI: how much green vegetation is visible?
ndvi.body: An index derived from reflected light. A higher value often indicates more green vegetation, but comparisons depend on season and land cover. It is not a yield estimate.

ndmi.title: NDMI: what does the moisture signal mean?
ndmi.body: An index sensitive to moisture in vegetation. It is not a soil-moisture percentage, a groundwater measurement or a direct instruction to irrigate.

confidence.title: Does high confidence mean the conclusion is certain?
confidence.body: No. Data quality concerns the observations; model confidence concerns the evidence behind an estimate. Neither is a guarantee of crop health or ecological suitability.

missing.title: Why is my area missing or a value blank?
missing.body: The monitoring window does not cover all of Dhofar. Clouds and limited usable observations can also prevent an assessment. A blank value means unavailable, not zero or healthy.

updates.title: Does refreshing images update the readings?
updates.body: No. The image button searches the scene catalogue. Agricultural readings update only after the processing job accepts new evidence and publishes a complete release.

pests.title: Can the satellite identify a pest or disease?
pests.body: The platform can flag possible stress, but cannot confirm a pest or disease. Optional field observations can help investigate; do not choose a pesticide from the satellite flag alone.

mountains.title: Are mountain restoration results the same as farm results?
mountains.body: No. Mountain and khareef restoration use a separate evidence path. A seasonal guide is not a live forecast, and seed-broadcast timing remains deferred when evidence is insufficient.
